title: Cap. 7 Rat. 10: without absolute elect-saving will grace no better prepared than in Adam
pass_a_gloss: Ratio 10. If Christ should not have offered himself to God the Father with a certain peculiar and absolute will of redeeming and efficaciously saving the elect by the merit of his death; then efficacious grace and eternal life would not otherwise have been prepared, or given to any human beings in Christ, than it was in Adam. For the possibility of having grace and eternal life under a condition hanging on our free choice was granted to the human race in the first Adam.
pass_b_english: Ratio 10. If Christ did not offer himself to the Father with a peculiar absolute will to redeem and save the elect efficaciously by his death's merit, then efficacious grace and eternal life would be prepared or given to no one in Christ on any better footing than they were in Adam. The first Adam already gave the race the chance of grace and eternal life under a condition that hangs on our free choice.
source_text: Rat. 10. Si Christus non obtulerit seipsum Deo Patri cum peculiari quadam, & absoluta voluntate redimendi & efficaciter salvandi electos merito mortis suae; tum gratia efficax & vita aeterna non aliter praeparata esset, aut donata ullis hominibus in Christo, quam fuit in Adamo. Possibilitas enim habendi gratiam & vitam aeternam sub conditione ex libero arbitrio nostro pendente, in primo Adamo fuit concessa humano generi.
